surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the reduction of Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 using 1,1-dimethylhydrazine (DMH) as a coreactant. The process occurs in two steps: first, the surface-bound Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 reacts with DMH, and then the surface is purged with N2. The reaction is self-limited, with a growth rate of 0.42 Å/cycle within an ALD window of 200–210 °C. The mechanism is characterized by the formation of Ru metal through the reduction of Ru precursors by DMH, leading to the deposition of Ru films with minimal nucleation delay.
evidence: The surface reaction mechanism is described in the text as follows: 'Experiments to probe a self-limited behavior were first carried out at 200 °C on TiN substrates. Using a recipe of Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 (variable)/N2 purge (20 s)/DMH (0.2 s)/N2 purge (20 s), a constant growth rate of 0.42 Å/cycle was found at ≥3.0 s pulse lengths of Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 [Fig. 1(a)]. The films were of uniform thickness by SEM and indicate a very different growth behavior with Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 and DMH, compared to Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 alone as described above. The greatly enhanced growth rate and film uniformity observed with Ru(DMBD)(CO)3 and DMH imply a key role of DMH in the growth process, but thermal decomposition may provide Ru seed crystals or more reactive Ru compounds that assist the film growth.'
